_README: KAMO daily reminder — live configuration. Edit this file, commit, push: GitHub Pages
serves it in a couple of minutes and every device picks it up on its next launch. No
build, no App Store review.
enabled:false is the kill switch. It does not merely stop scheduling — it CANCELS what
is already pending, so the fortnight of reminders sitting in the queue stops too.
Anything invalid here is ignored field by field and falls back to what shipped in the
binary, so a typo costs you that one value, never the feature. Ranges are clamped:
hours 0-23 (start must be <= end), horizonDays 1-21, settleMs 0-15000.
The 7 message lines rotate by calendar date. requiresHistory:true lines are swapped for
firstHide until the user has finished at least one hide.
settingsRecovery is now ON, and the condition it was waiting for has been met.
It shipped dark with an explicit trigger: turn it on once daily_reminder_optin_outcome
shows how many people are stuck behind a denial. Through August that number was zero —
nobody had reached Apple's prompt at all, so a dialog offering a trip to Settings would
have been offered to nobody. Since sessionsBeforeAsk went to 1 the prompt is actually
being reached, and `already_denied` now appears daily. iOS never re-asks after a Don't
Allow, so this dialog is the ONLY way back for those people. Easy to overdo: it is
capped by maxSoftAsks and minDaysBetweenAsks like every other ask here.
sessionsBeforeAsk WAS 2, AND IT WAS THE WHOLE FEATURE'S OFF SWITCH.
August: 106 asks reached maybeAskPermission and 99 of them died on `not_eligible_yet`
— 93%. Five more hit the cooldown, two declined the soft-ask, and not one person ever
opted in. daily_reminder_scheduled has never been ingested by Amplitude at all: no
device has ever had a single reminder queued, on any build, since the feature shipped.
The cause is arithmetic. initNotifications does sessions+1 at launch, so a first
session reads sessions=1, and the gate is `sessions < sessionsBeforeAsk`. At 2, being
asked required coming back a SECOND day — from an audience that arrives on a TikTok ad
and overwhelmingly does not return. The reminder existed to cause that return and was
gated behind it.
1 keeps every part of the design that was actually load-bearing: the ask still only
fires from onHideFinished, i.e. after a finished hide, never on a cold launch, still
behind our own soft dialog, and a Not now is still re-askable. The only thing dropped
is the requirement to have already come back.
THE WHOLE DIALOG WAS REWRITTEN ON 2026-08-15, AND THE 08-14 READ BELOW IS ABANDONED.
Say it plainly so nobody mistakes the note under this one for a week of evidence: the
08-14 askBody lived for ONE DAY. It was not cut short out of impatience — it was posted
the day before seek traffic went 20x and the audience flipped from TikTok installs to
organic virality. A before/after straddling that does not measure a sentence, it measures
a different population. The note below anticipated the weekday mix moving the
denominator; it did not anticipate that.
What replaces it, and why each word. TITLE leads with the feeling instead of the
mechanism: only a quarter to a third of seekers ever find the kamo, so the thing being
offered is watching somebody lose. `Know when they try to find you` described a feature.
BODY keeps the daily nudge — a dialog that hides what the permission is for earns a
Settings-off a week later — but it now says `your kamo`, which is the brand's own noun
(see the copy rule; `body` is banned everywhere, including the TikTok ad classifier's
sake). YES goes from `Turn it on`, which describes a switch, to `Notify me`, which
describes the outcome.
EVERY THRESHOLD IN THIS FILE IS FROZEN ON PURPOSE. sessionsBeforeAsk, maxSoftAsks and
minDaysBetweenAsks decide WHO is asked; the four strings above decide how many say yes.
Only the strings moved, so the next read is copy v2 against copy v1 and stays clean —
just with a one-day v1. Judge on daily_reminder_optin_outcome: (system_granted +
system_denied) over soft_declined + both. Baseline to beat: 29-30%.
--- superseded, kept for the reasoning only ---
askBody IS THE ONE THING CHANGED ON 2026-08-14, AND IT IS CHANGED ALONE.
Week of 08-10, uniques: soft_declined 281, system_granted 83, system_denied 33. Our own
dialog converts at 29%; iOS, once reached, says yes 72% of the time. So the binding
constraint is not Apple and never was — it is this sentence.
It used to read: the moment someone opens your challenge, AND a nudge once a day to hide
another. Two promises, and the second is a chore. A daily reminder is a thing you agree
to endure; someone hunting the kamo you hid is a thing you want to know. Leading with the
chore spends the appetite the first half just created.
The daily nudge is still promised, because it still happens and a dialog that hides what
the permission is for earns a Settings-off a week later. It is reframed rather than
dropped: your turn to hide, not a reminder to do homework.
NOTHING ELSE MOVED IN THIS FILE ON PURPOSE. sessionsBeforeAsk, maxSoftAsks and
minDaysBetweenAsks decide WHO gets asked; this decides how many of them say yes. Move
both at once and neither number can be read afterwards. Judge it on
daily_reminder_optin_outcome: (system_granted + system_denied) over soft_declined + both,
against the 29% above. Wait for a full week — this audience arrives on ads and the
weekday mix moves the denominator.
